data.name: Security_AttrSuperuser
data.comment: Label of the superuser attribute of a role: a row in the Roles tab's details and a check box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_AttrInherit
data.comment: Label of the inherit attribute of a role (it uses the privileges of the groups it belongs to): a row in the Roles tab's details and a check box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_AttrCreateDb
data.comment: Label of the attribute that lets a role create databases: a row in the Roles tab's details and a check box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_AttrCreateRole
data.comment: Label of the attribute that lets a role create other roles: a row in the Roles tab's details and a check box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_AttrReplication
data.comment: Label of the replication attribute of a role: a row in the Roles tab's details and a check box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_AttrBypassRls
data.comment: Label of the attribute that makes a role skip row-level security: a row in the Roles tab's details and a check box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_DetailConnectionLimit
data.comment: Roles tab, role details: label of the row with the most connections the role may hold.

data.name: Security_DetailComment
data.comment: Roles tab, role details: label of the row with the role's comment.

data.name: Security_GroupPrivilegesNeedSetRole
data.value: los privilegios de grupo requieren SET ROLE
data.comment: Roles tab, role details: small note beside Inherit = no. SET ROLE is SQL.

data.name: Security_Yes
data.comment: Roles tab, role details: the value of a yes-or-no attribute that is on.

data.name: Security_No
data.comment: Roles tab, role details: the value of a yes-or-no attribute that is off.

data.name: Security_NoLimit
data.comment: A role has no connection limit. Shown in the Roles tab's details and as the placeholder of the connection limit box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_NoExpiry
data.comment: A role's password never expires. Shown in the Roles tab's details and as the placeholder of the date box in the role dialog.

data.name: Security_RoleScriptTabTitle
data.comment: Title of the query tab that opens with a role's CREATE ROLE statement. {name} is the role's name, such as app_ro.

data.name: Security_RoleNew
data.comment: Title of the role dialog when it creates a role.

data.name: Security_RoleAlter
data.comment: Title of the role dialog when it changes a role. {name} is the role's name, such as app_ro. Keep the quotation marks around it.

data.name: Security_RoleName
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals label of the role name box.

data.name: Security_RoleNamePlaceholder
data.comment: Role dialog: example role name shown dimmed in the empty name box. An identifier; a translation may keep it.

data.name: Security_CanLogIn
data.comment: Role dialog: check box that lets the role log in.

data.name: Security_Password
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals label of the password box.

data.name: Security_PasswordConfirm
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals label of the box that repeats the password.

data.name: Security_Attributes
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals heading above the attribute check boxes.

data.name: Security_InheritTip
data.value: Desactivado significa que el rol debe hacer SET ROLE antes de que se apliquen los privilegios de un grupo
data.comment: Role dialog: tooltip of the Inherit check box. SET ROLE is SQL.

data.name: Security_BypassRlsTip
data.value: Omite siempre todas las políticas de seguridad a nivel de fila
data.comment: Role dialog: tooltip of the Bypass RLS check box.

data.name: Security_ConnectionLimit
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals label of the box with the most connections the role may hold.

data.name: Security_ValidUntil
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals label of the date box where the role's password expires.

data.name: Security_BuiltinRoles
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals heading above the check boxes for roles PostgreSQL ships with, such as pg_read_all_data.

data.name: Security_Comment
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals label of the comment box.

data.name: Security_CommentPlaceholder
data.comment: Role dialog: placeholder of the comment box.

data.name: Security_GeneratedSql
data.comment: Role dialog: small capitals heading above the SQL statement the dialog will run.

data.name: Security_HintReadAllData
data.value: SELECT en todas las tablas, vistas y secuencias, de todos los esquemas
data.comment: Role dialog: hint beside the pg_read_all_data check box. SELECT is SQL.

data.name: Security_HintWriteAllData
data.value: INSERT, UPDATE y DELETE en todas las tablas
data.comment: Role dialog: hint beside the pg_write_all_data check box. INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE are SQL.

data.name: Security_HintMonitor
data.value: leer las estadísticas y las vistas de monitorización sin ser superusuario
data.comment: Role dialog: hint beside the pg_monitor check box.

data.name: Security_HintLoginRole
data.comment: Role dialog: hint beside a role in the MEMBER OF list: this role can log in.

data.name: Security_HintGroupRole
data.comment: Role dialog: hint beside a role in the MEMBER OF list: this role cannot log in, so it is a group.

data.name: Security_NeedsName
data.comment: Role dialog: validation message under the form.

data.name: Security_PasswordsDiffer
data.comment: Role dialog: validation message under the form.

data.name: Security_PasswordNeedsPg10
data.value: Establecer una contraseña requiere PostgreSQL 10 o posterior. Hazlo con \password de psql en este servidor.
data.comment: Role dialog: validation message under the form, shown on a server older than PostgreSQL 10. psql's \password is a psql command and stays as written.

data.name: Security_NothingChanged
data.comment: Role dialog: validation message under the form while nothing differs from the saved role.

data.name: Security_LoginWithoutPassword
data.value: Este rol puede iniciar sesión pero no tiene contraseña. Eso solo funciona si pg_hba.conf lo autentica de otra forma.
data.comment: Role dialog: warning under the form. pg_hba.conf is the name of a server configuration file.

data.name: Security_NonAsciiPassword
data.value: Esta contraseña tiene caracteres fuera de ASCII. Algunos clientes de PostgreSQL los normalizan antes de iniciar sesión y pgNimbus no puede hacer lo mismo aquí, así que podrían rechazarla. Una contraseña ASCII siempre funciona.
data.comment: Role dialog: warning under the form when the password has characters outside plain ASCII (accented letters and similar). ASCII means the basic Latin letters, digits and punctuation.

data.name: Security_DropWindowTitle
data.comment: Window title of the dialog that drops a role. Keep the product name pgNimbus.

data.name: Security_DropHint
data.value: Un rol que posee objetos o tiene privilegios no se puede eliminar sin más. Reasignar antes sus objetos y quitar sus privilegios es lo que hace que DROP ROLE funcione.
data.comment: Drop role dialog: explanation under the role's name. DROP ROLE is SQL.

data.name: Security_OwnedHeader
data.comment: Drop role dialog: heading above the list of objects the role owns, before the list has loaded.

data.name: Security_OwnedHeaderCount
data.comment: Drop role dialog: heading above the list of objects the role owns. {count} is how many, such as 3.

data.name: Security_GrantsHeader
data.comment: Drop role dialog: heading above the list of privileges granted to the role, before the list has loaded.

data.name: Security_GrantsHeaderCount
data.comment: Drop role dialog: heading above the list of privileges granted to the role. {count} is how many, such as 3.

data.name: Security_GrantsHeaderTruncated
data.comment: Drop role dialog: heading above the list of privileges granted to the role when the list was cut at a limit. {count} is that limit, such as 200; the plus sign means more exist.

data.name: Security_ColKind
data.comment: Drop role dialog: column header of the kind of object (table, view, schema …).

data.name: Security_ColObject
data.comment: Drop role dialog: column header of the object's name.

data.name: Security_OwnsNothing
data.value: No posee nada en esta base de datos.
data.comment: Drop role dialog: shown in place of the list of owned objects when it is empty.

data.name: Security_HoldsNoPrivileges
data.value: No tiene privilegios en esta base de datos.
data.comment: Drop role dialog: shown in place of the list of granted privileges when it is empty.

data.name: Security_ReassignTo
data.comment: Drop role dialog: label of the drop-down that picks the role that takes over the objects.

data.name: Security_ReassignNobody
data.comment: Drop role dialog: the drop-down choice that gives the objects to no one, so they are deleted.

data.name: Security_GrantMembership
data.value: Concederme las pertenencias que necesita el script
data.comment: Drop role dialog: check box text.

data.name: Security_GrantMembershipTip
data.value: REASSIGN OWNED y DROP OWNED requieren los privilegios del rol que se vacía. El script te los concede y te devuelve el que sobrevive al rol.
data.comment: Drop role dialog: tooltip of the check box. REASSIGN OWNED and DROP OWNED are SQL statements.

data.name: Security_WillDeleteOwned
data.value: Sin un sucesor indicado, DROP OWNED elimina los objetos de este rol en lugar de transferirlos.
data.comment: Drop role dialog: warning shown when no role is chosen to take over the objects. DROP OWNED is SQL.

data.name: Security_DropCurrentDatabaseOnly
data.value: REASSIGN OWNED y DROP OWNED actúan solo en la base de datos actual. Si este rol posee objetos en otras bases de datos, ejecuta el script de nuevo conectado a cada una antes de que el rol se pueda eliminar.
data.comment: Drop role dialog: note under the form. REASSIGN OWNED and DROP OWNED are SQL statements.

data.name: Security_OpenInEditor
data.comment: Button in the drop role dialog and the bulk grant dialog: opens the generated script in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_OpenInEditorDropTip
data.value: Ejecútalo tú — y vuelve a ejecutarlo en cada otra base de datos donde este rol posea objetos
data.comment: Drop role dialog: tooltip of the Open in editor button.

data.name: Security_RunIt
data.comment: Drop role dialog: the button that runs the generated script now.

data.name: Security_DropRoleTabTitle
data.comment: Title of the query tab that opens with the drop-role script. {name} is the role's name, such as legacy_etl.

data.name: Security_KindTable
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a table.

data.name: Security_KindPartitionedTable
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a partitioned table.

data.name: Security_KindView
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a view.

data.name: Security_KindMaterializedView
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a materialized view.

data.name: Security_KindSequence
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a sequence.

data.name: Security_KindForeignTable
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a foreign table.

data.name: Security_KindSchema
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a schema.

data.name: Security_KindProcedure
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a procedure.

data.name: Security_KindFunction
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a function.

data.name: Security_KindType
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a data type.

data.name: Security_KindDatabase
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column: a database.

data.name: Security_KindPrivilegeOnTable
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column of the privileges list: a privilege granted on a table.

data.name: Security_KindPrivilegeOnSchema
data.comment: Drop role dialog, Kind column of the privileges list: a privilege granted on a schema.

data.name: Security_BulkWindowTitle
data.comment: Window title of the bulk grant dialog. Keep the product name pgNimbus.

data.name: Security_BulkTitle
data.value: Dar acceso a un rol a todo un esquema
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: heading.

data.name: Security_BulkHint
data.value: El script siempre empieza con USAGE sobre el propio esquema — sin él, cada concesión de tabla de abajo no sirve de nada. Desde aquí no se ejecuta nada: el script se abre en el editor para que lo leas y lo ejecutes.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: explanation under the heading. USAGE is a SQL privilege name and stays as written.

data.name: Security_Schema
data.comment: Label or placeholder of a schema picker: the bulk grant dialog, the Permissions tab and the Row-level security tab.

data.name: Security_Grantee
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: label of the picker for the role that gets access.

data.name: Security_SchemaPlaceholder
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: placeholder of the schema picker.

data.name: Security_GranteePlaceholder
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: placeholder of the role picker.

data.name: Security_Preset
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: label of the picker for how much access to give.

data.name: Security_PresetReadOnly
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: name of a preset in the picker.

data.name: Security_PresetReadOnlyDescription
data.value: SELECT en todas las tablas y vistas, más USAGE y SELECT en secuencias.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: what the Read only preset does. SELECT and USAGE are SQL privilege names.

data.name: Security_PresetReadWrite
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: name of a preset in the picker.

data.name: Security_PresetReadWriteDescription
data.value: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE y DELETE en tablas, más USAGE, SELECT y UPDATE en secuencias.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: what the Read and write preset does. SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and USAGE are SQL privilege names.

data.name: Security_PresetFull
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: name of a preset in the picker.

data.name: Security_PresetFullDescription
data.value: ALL PRIVILEGES en tablas, secuencias y funciones, más CREATE en el propio esquema.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: what the Everything in the schema preset does. ALL PRIVILEGES and CREATE are SQL.

data.name: Security_PresetRevokeAll
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: name of a preset in the picker.

data.name: Security_PresetRevokeAllDescription
data.value: REVOKE ALL en tablas, secuencias, funciones y el esquema — y también en los privilegios por defecto.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: what the Revoke everything preset does. REVOKE ALL is SQL.

data.name: Security_IncludeFuture
data.value: Cubrir también los objetos creados después (añade ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES)
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: check box text. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is a SQL statement.

data.name: Security_IncludeFutureHint
data.value: Sin esto, la concesión solo alcanza las tablas, vistas y secuencias que existen en el momento de ejecutarla. Lo que cree una migración posterior no queda cubierto.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: explanation under the check box about objects created later.

data.name: Security_CreatedBy
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: label of the picker for the role that will create the future objects.

data.name: Security_CreatedByPlaceholder
data.value: El rol que creará los objetos
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: placeholder of the Created by picker.

data.name: Security_CreatedByWarning
data.value: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES se asocia al rol que crea un objeto, no al esquema donde acaba. Si apuntas al creador equivocado, se ejecuta sin errores y no hace nada — indica el rol con el que se conectan tus migraciones.
data.comment: Bulk grant dialog: warning under the Created by picker. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is a SQL statement.

data.name: Security_GrantsTabTitle
data.comment: Title of the query tab that opens with a GRANT script. {name} is a schema or an object, such as sales.orders.

data.name: Security_ObjectFilterPlaceholder
data.comment: Permissions tab: placeholder of the box that filters the list of objects.

data.name: Security_BulkGrant
data.comment: Permissions tab: button that opens the bulk grant dialog.

data.name: Security_BulkGrantTip
data.value: Da acceso a un rol a todo un esquema, incluidos los objetos creados después
data.comment: Permissions tab: tooltip of the Bulk grant button.

data.name: Security_EditGrants
data.comment: Permissions tab: toggle button that lets the cells of the matrix be clicked to stage changes.

data.name: Security_EditGrantsTip
data.value: Haz clic en las celdas para dejar pendiente un GRANT o REVOKE; no se ejecuta nada hasta que revises el script
data.comment: Permissions tab: tooltip of the Edit grants button. GRANT and REVOKE are SQL.

data.name: Security_ReviewChanges
data.comment: Permissions tab: button that opens the staged GRANT and REVOKE statements in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_RoleFilterPlaceholder
data.comment: Permissions tab: placeholder of the box that filters the roles in the matrix.

data.name: Security_BuiltinRolesToggle
data.comment: Permissions tab: toggle that also shows the roles PostgreSQL ships with.

data.name: Security_BuiltinRolesToggleTip
data.value: Mostrar los roles pg_* que creó initdb
data.comment: Permissions tab: tooltip of the Built-in roles toggle. initdb is the PostgreSQL program that creates a cluster.

data.name: Security_ColRoleCaps
data.comment: Permissions tab: small capitals header of the role names above the matrix.

data.name: Security_ColHowCaps
data.comment: Permissions tab: small capitals header of the column that says how each role gets its privileges (directly, inherited, owner …).

data.name: Security_ColumnGrants
data.comment: Permissions tab: small capitals heading above the privileges granted on single columns.

data.name: Security_KindOptionTable
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionSequence
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionSchema
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionDatabase
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionFunction
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_KindOptionType
data.comment: Permissions tab: choice in the picker of what kind of object to show.

data.name: Security_NoPendingChanges
data.comment: Permissions tab: label beside Edit grants while nothing is staged.

data.name: Security_PendingChanges_one
data.comment: Permissions tab: label beside Edit grants. Plural. {count} is how many changes are staged, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PendingChanges_other
data.comment: Permissions tab: label beside Edit grants. Plural. {count} is how many changes are staged, such as 3.

data.name: Security_DefaultAclNote
data.value: Nunca se ha ejecutado GRANT ni REVOKE sobre este objeto. {owner} es su propietario y tiene todos los privilegios; los demás solo tienen lo que Postgres concede por defecto para este tipo de objeto.
data.comment: Permissions tab: banner shown when the object's privileges were never changed. GRANT and REVOKE are SQL. {owner} is the owning role's name, such as postgres.

data.name: Security_CellTip
data.comment: Permissions tab: tooltip of a cell of the matrix. {privilege} is the SQL privilege such as SELECT; {explanation} says why the role has it or not, such as inherited from readers.

data.name: Security_CellTipPendingRevoke
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when a REVOKE is staged for it. REVOKE is SQL.

data.name: Security_CellTipPendingGrant
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when a GRANT is staged for it. GRANT is SQL.

data.name: Security_CellTipNotRevocable
data.value: Ser propietario o superusuario no son concesiones, así que no se puede revocar.
data.comment: Permissions tab: second line of a cell's tooltip when the privilege comes from owning the object or being a superuser.

data.name: Security_SourceSuperuser
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has everything because it is a superuser.

data.name: Security_SourceOwner
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has everything because it owns the object.

data.name: Security_SourceVia
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the role has the privileges through its membership in another role. {role} is that group role, such as readers.

data.name: Security_SourceDirect
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the privilege was granted to the role itself.

data.name: Security_SourcePublic
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the privilege was granted to PUBLIC, the SQL keyword for every role. A translation may keep it.

data.name: Security_SourceUnknown
data.comment: Permissions tab, HOW column: the server says the role has the privilege but the catalog does not show why.

data.name: Security_PublicGrantee
data.comment: The grantee shown for a privilege or policy that applies to every role: the SQL keyword PUBLIC. A translation may keep it. A role that is merely named PUBLIC is shown in quotation marks by the app, so the two can be told apart.

data.name: Security_ExplainNone
data.comment: Why a role does or does not have a privilege (tooltip of a matrix cell, and part of the sentence under the matrix): it was not granted.

data.name: Security_ExplainDirectBy
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to the role itself. {grantor} is the role that ran the GRANT, such as postgres.

data.name: Security_ExplainDirect
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to the role itself, by a role we cannot name.

data.name: Security_ExplainInherited
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: through its membership in a group role. {role} is that group, such as readers.

data.name: Security_ExplainPublic
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it was granted to PUBLIC, the SQL keyword for every role.

data.name: Security_ExplainOwner
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it owns the object.

data.name: Security_ExplainSuperuser
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: it is a superuser.

data.name: Security_ExplainUnknown
data.value: concedido, origen no visible desde aquí
data.comment: Why a role has a privilege: the server says yes but the catalog the app can read does not explain it.

data.name: Security_ListSeparator
data.comment: Separator between the items of a list of privileges, such as SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE. Put a space after it if your language uses one.

data.name: Security_ListAnd
data.comment: Joins a list of privileges with and: {head} is the items before the last one, joined by the list separator (SELECT, INSERT), {last} is the last one (UPDATE).

data.name: Security_ListOr
data.comment: Joins a list of privileges with or: {head} is the items before the last one, joined by the list separator (SELECT, INSERT), {last} is the last one (UPDATE).

data.name: Security_SentenceNone
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {object} the object such as sales.orders.

data.name: Security_SentenceNoneBlocked
data.value: {role} no tiene privilegios sobre {object}. {role} tampoco tiene USAGE sobre el esquema {schema}, lo que bloquea el acceso a todo lo que contiene.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {object} the object such as sales.orders, {schema} its schema. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlocked_one
data.value: {role} tiene {privileges} sobre {object} — {explanation} — pero no puede usarlo: le falta USAGE sobre el esquema {schema}, que todo objeto de él necesita primero.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable. {role} is a role name, {privileges} a list such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object, {explanation} why the role has them, {schema} the schema. "them" is the privileges. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlocked_other
data.value: {role} tiene {privileges} sobre {object} — {explanation} — pero no puede usarlos: le falta USAGE sobre el esquema {schema}, que todo objeto de él necesita primero.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable. {role} is a role name, {privileges} a list such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object, {explanation} why the role has them, {schema} the schema. "them" is the privileges. USAGE is a SQL privilege name.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlockedDenied_one
data.value: {role} tiene {privileges} sobre {object} — {explanation} — pero no puede usarlo: le falta USAGE sobre el esquema {schema}, que todo objeto de él necesita primero. Tampoco tiene la concesión {denied}.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable, and others are missing. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceBlocked_other, plus {denied}, the missing privileges as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_SentenceBlockedDenied_other
data.value: {role} tiene {privileges} sobre {object} — {explanation} — pero no puede usarlos: le falta USAGE sobre el esquema {schema}, que todo objeto de él necesita primero. Tampoco tiene la concesión {denied}.
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Plural: several privileges are held but unusable, and others are missing. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceBlocked_other, plus {denied}, the missing privileges as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_SentenceCan
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. {role} is a role name, {privileges} what it can do as SQL verbs such as SELECT and INSERT, {object} the object such as sales.orders, {explanation} why, such as inherited from readers.

data.name: Security_SentenceCanCannot
data.comment: Permissions tab, sentence under the matrix. Same placeholders as Security_SentenceCan, plus {denied}, what the role cannot do as a list joined with or, such as INSERT or UPDATE.

data.name: Security_CopyAsSql
data.comment: Default privileges tab: button that opens the selected row's ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_CopyAsSqlTip
data.value: Abre en una pestaña nueva del editor la sentencia ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES que representa esta fila
data.comment: Default privileges tab: tooltip of the Copy as SQL button. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES is SQL.

data.name: Security_ColCreatedBy
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the role that will create the objects the default applies to.

data.name: Security_ColInSchema
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the schema the default applies in.

data.name: Security_ColAppliesTo
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the kind of object the default applies to (tables, sequences …).

data.name: Security_ColGrantee
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the role that gets the privileges.

data.name: Security_ColPrivileges
data.comment: Default privileges tab: column header of the list of privileges.

data.name: Security_AllSchemas
data.comment: Shown instead of a schema name in the Default privileges tab (the default applies in every schema) and as the first choice of the schema filter in the Row-level security tab. Keep the parentheses.

data.name: Security_AppliesToTables
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to tables.

data.name: Security_AppliesToSequences
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to sequences.

data.name: Security_AppliesToFunctions
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to functions.

data.name: Security_AppliesToTypes
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to data types.

data.name: Security_AppliesToSchemas
data.comment: Default privileges tab, Applies to column: the default applies to schemas.

data.name: Security_NoDefaultPrivileges
data.comment: Default privileges tab: heading shown when there are none.

data.name: Security_NoDefaultPrivilegesHint
data.value: Todo objeto creado a partir de ahora llevará solo los valores integrados: su propietario recibe todo, PUBLIC recibe EXECUTE en funciones y USAGE en tipos, y nada en absoluto en tablas y secuencias.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: explanation under the heading shown when there are none. PUBLIC, EXECUTE and USAGE are SQL words and stay as written.

data.name: Security_DefaultsNoteExisting
data.value: No afectan a los objetos que ya existen. Se aplican a los objetos creados a partir de ahora, por eso hacen falta tanto un GRANT … ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA … como un privilegio por defecto: ninguno sustituye al otro.
data.comment: Default privileges tab: first note under the list. The GRANT statement is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_DefaultsNoteCreator
data.value: Se asocian al rol que crea el objeto, no al esquema donde acaba. Un privilegio por defecto definido para el creador equivocado se ejecuta sin errores y no hace nada, la causa más común de «lo definí y nada cambió».
data.comment: Default privileges tab: second note under the list.

data.name: Security_DefaultPrivilegesTabTitle
data.comment: Title of the query tab that opens with an ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES statement. {owner} is the role that creates the objects, such as app_rw.

data.name: Security_SchemaFilterTip
data.value: Solo se listan los esquemas que tienen seguridad a nivel de fila en algún sitio
data.comment: Row-level security tab: tooltip of the schema filter.

data.name: Security_CopyPolicyAsSql
data.comment: Row-level security tab: button that opens the selected policy's CREATE POLICY statement in a new query tab.

data.name: Security_CopyPolicyAsSqlTip
data.value: Abre en una pestaña nueva del editor la sentencia CREATE POLICY de la política seleccionada — Postgres no puede cambiar en el sitio el comando ni la permisividad de una política, así que se edita volviéndola a crear
data.comment: Row-level security tab: tooltip of the Copy policy as SQL button. CREATE POLICY is SQL.

data.name: Security_PoliciesInert
data.comment: Row-level security tab, list of tables: warning on a table that has policies but row-level security is switched off. RLS means row-level security.

data.name: Security_PoliciesDoNothing
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading of a warning about a table whose policies have no effect.

data.name: Security_PoliciesDoNothingHint
data.value: La seguridad a nivel de fila nunca se activó en esta tabla, así que todas las políticas de abajo son inertes y todos los roles leen todas las filas. Escribir políticas no la activa — ALTER TABLE … ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY sí.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: explanation of the warning. The ALTER TABLE statement is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_YouBypass
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading of a warning that the connected role is not subject to the policies.

data.name: Security_DeniesEverything
data.value: La seguridad a nivel de fila está activada y esta tabla no tiene políticas, así que no devuelve filas a ningún rol que no la omita. Es el estado de denegación por defecto, no un error de configuración en sí.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: note on a table with row-level security on and no policies.

data.name: Security_PolicyAppliesTo
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label before the roles a policy applies to.

data.name: Security_PolicyUsing
data.value: USING — qué filas existentes son visibles
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label above a policy's USING expression. USING is the SQL keyword and stays first.

data.name: Security_PolicyWithCheck
data.value: WITH CHECK — qué filas nuevas o actualizadas se permiten
data.comment: Row-level security tab: label above a policy's WITH CHECK expression. WITH CHECK is the SQL keyword and stays first.

data.name: Security_NoPolicies
data.comment: Row-level security tab: shown in the details of a table without policies.

data.name: Security_NoRlsTables
data.value: Ninguna tabla usa seguridad por fila.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: heading shown when no table has row-level security or a policy.

data.name: Security_NoRlsTablesHint
data.value: Las tablas aparecen aquí en cuanto tienen la seguridad de fila activada o llevan una política, en cualquier orden.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: explanation under the heading shown when no table has row-level security.

data.name: Security_RlsEnabledForce
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is on and also applies to the table's owner (SQL option FORCE).

data.name: Security_RlsEnabled
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is on.

data.name: Security_RlsNotEnabled
data.comment: Row-level security tab: state of a table. Row-level security is off.

data.name: Security_PolicyCount_one
data.comment: Row-level security tab: how many policies a table has. Plural. {count} is the number, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PolicyCount_other
data.comment: Row-level security tab: how many policies a table has. Plural. {count} is the number, such as 3.

data.name: Security_PolicyForEveryone
data.comment: Row-level security tab: the policy applies to every role (the SQL keyword PUBLIC).

data.name: Security_BypassUnknown
data.value: {role} ve todas las filas de esta tabla, digan lo que digan las políticas de abajo. No se pudieron leer sus atributos de rol, así que es un rol superuser o BYPASSRLS (que omite todas las tablas, siempre) o propietario de una tabla que no es FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. BYPASSRLS and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_BypassSuperuser
data.value: {role} es superusuario, así que omite la seguridad a nivel de fila en todas las tablas del clúster. Es incondicional: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY no le aplica las políticas. Prueba estas políticas con el rol con el que se conecta tu aplicación.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is SQL and stays as written.

data.name: Security_BypassAttribute
data.value: {role} tiene el atributo BYPASSRLS, así que omite la seguridad a nivel de fila en todas las tablas, siempre. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY no le aplica las políticas. Prueba estas políticas con el rol con el que se conecta tu aplicación.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. BYPASSRLS and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_BypassOwner
data.value: {role} es propietario de esta tabla, o miembro del rol que lo es, y la tabla no es FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY — así que las políticas de abajo no se le aplican, aunque sí a todos los demás roles. ALTER TABLE … FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY hace que se apliquen también al propietario.
data.comment: Row-level security tab: warning body. {role} is the connected role. FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the ALTER TABLE statement are SQL and stay as written.

data.name: Security_ObjectDropped
data.value: {object} ya no existe — se eliminó después de construir la lista de objetos.
data.comment: Error line of the Roles and Permissions window. {object} is the name of the object, such as sales.orders.
